review.summary: Phase 8 (Qualification and delivery) holds up under inspection rather than resting on prose. The recorded gate `docs/checks/phase-08.json` contains exactly the 77 commands that `tools/check_phase.py:138-167` defines for phase 8 (I recomputed the cumulative set: 7 + 19 → 26 at phase 3, 29, 33, 36, 48 at phase 7, + 29 new = 77), every record has `exit_code: 0`, and the report is bound to source `ce2a547a…` with `source_unchanged: true` and `passed: true`; a pattern search for a non-zero exit code across `docs/checks/` matches only the deliberately preserved `phase-08-failed-attempt-0{1,2,3,4}*.json`. The underlying checks are real work. `scripts/check-dependencies.py` clones/fetches authoritative RustSec, pins cargo-audit 0.22.2 and cargo-deny 0.20.2 by binary SHA-256, refuses any advisory ignore/license exception/relaxed source, and recorded 0 vulnerabilities, empty warnings, 206 packages, `freshHead: true`. `scripts/check-package.py` builds the real `.crate`, rejects unsafe/out-of-policy members before extraction without `tar.extractall`, requires the self-contained `src/fixtures/model-regressions.json` corpus (closing the Phase-4 packaged-unit-test follow-up), and ran 145 minimal + 201 all-feature unit tests, examples, 11 doctests and the external 3,820-probe consumer against extracted archive contents at both 1.89.0 and 1.99.0. `contracts/qualification.json` projects all 448 frozen operations with implemented/contract-verified/option-parity complete, `liveVerified: 17`, `unexplainedGaps: 0`, and `tools/qualification.py:95-108,131-134` refuses constructor or family-wide promotion and forces reconciliation language on mixed observations. All five findings from attempt 1 are genuinely closed, each with new executable evidence: the tracing stress runner is now committed, gate-bound and documented with a reproduction command (`scripts/check-tracing-stress.py`, `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md:61-87`, 100/100 processes × 201 tests, receipt bound to source `ce2a547a…`); the credential scanner is committed, gate-invoked, documented in `docs/SECURITY.md:67-122` and covered by 27 `test_auxiliary_evidence.py` cases; `tools/live_evidence.py:204-231` now retains every observation and selects the worst outcome by `FAILURE_PRIORITY` (tests `test_success_cannot_hide_a_failure_in_either_observation_order`, `test_cleanup_failure_or_success_never_hides_its_conflicting_probe`); bounded closed-vocabulary `rejectionDetails` were added with 2 dedicated tests; and the rustdoc boundary is now explicit with `#![warn(missing_docs)]` in `scanner.rs:1`, `no_run` examples on all eight product facades and a documented coverage boundary in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:70-113`. Security posture is strong: credential-free verification, `PANW_/AIRS_/SCM_` scrubbing in every runner, 0600 private outputs, `unsafe_code = "forbid"`, no placeholders anywhere in `crates/`, and the `json_decode.rs` reserved-protocol-key boundary is a bounded non-recursive guard whose only non-test `serde_json::from_*` siblings (`streaming/sse.rs:120,144`) read keys as `String` and values as `RawValue`/`IgnoredAny` and so cannot trigger `Value` protocol coercion. Platform, CI, release and README text consistently separate implementation parity from offline contracts, live acceptance, compile-only targets and publication. The deduction is driven by one substantive gap: the controlled live mutation workflow has never succeeded. Across five consecutive receipts (attempts 02–06) `iam.scopes.create` and `gateway.workspaces.provision` both return 400 with `rejectionDetails {code: null, fields: []}`, the project's own matrix states a native request-shape defect is not excluded, and as a consequence `iam.scopes.get/update/delete`, absence verification, workspace binding removal and archival confirmation have no live execution at all and `cleanupState` is trivially `not_needed` — for the phase whose evidence line reads "controlled live acceptance and cleanup", that is a real shortfall, honestly recorded but unresolved and with no retained diagnostic to resolve it.

findings.description: The controlled live mutation workflow has never succeeded. `iam.scopes.create` (line 212) and `gateway.workspaces.provision` (line 232) both return 400 in attempt 06, and the same pair of 400s is recorded identically in attempts 02, 03, 04 and 05 (`docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-0{2,3,4,5}.json:212,228`); attempt 01 did not attempt them. The diagnostic added in response to the attempt-1 review yields nothing: `rejectionDetails` is `{code: null, fields: []}` because `crates/scm-sdk/examples/live_qualification.rs:170-173` derives it from `error.service_code()` and `error.problem()`, which were both empty. `tools/qualification.py:27` therefore records "its cause is unestablished and a native request-shape defect is not excluded" for two methods, one of which is `AIGatewayWorkspacesClient.provision` — one of only two Phase-7-owned workflows. The downstream effect is larger than two rows: because creation never succeeded, `iam.scopes.get`, `iam.scopes.update`, `iam.scopes.delete`, `iam.scopes.verify_absent`, `gateway.workspaces.get/delete` and `gateway.workspaces.verify_archived` have zero live observations, `cleanup` is `[]` and `cleanupState` is `not_needed` (lines 244, 33), so the entire mutation-and-cleanup half of the live acceptance milestone is unexercised. No private artifact can resolve the ambiguity either: `persist_recovery` (`crates/scm-sdk/examples/live_qualification.rs:448-458`) records intents and resource IDs, not rejected-response bodies, and a reproducible 400 across five runs on requests the SDK itself constructs is at least as consistent with a request-shape defect as with a service-side condition.
findings.required_fix: Retain a bounded, private (0600, outside git) diagnostic of the rejected request/response for 400/405/409/422 classes in the recovery snapshot written by `crates/scm-sdk/examples/live_qualification.rs:448`, re-run `tools/live_evidence.py --run` to determine whether `iam.scopes.create` and `gateway.workspaces.provision` are sending a malformed body, and either correct the native request shape and record a receipt that exercises create/read/update/delete/verify-absent plus workspace archival cleanup, or record in `docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md` the identified service-side cause with the evidence that excludes an SDK defect.

findings.description: `FEATURES["native-probes"]` and `FEATURES["probe-base"]` hardcode feature lists that are supposed to equal the derived export-probe gate. `tools/native_exports.py:455-456` computes `required_features` from the capability rows and emits the exact `#![cfg(all(...))]` header now present at `crates/scm-sdk/tests/native_export_probes.rs:2-13`, and `tools/test_native_exports.py:121-129` binds the generated gate to that union — but nothing asserts that the checker's `native-probes` string equals `contracts/native-exports.json` `probe.requiredFeatures` (lines 678-689). They happen to match today (10 features). If the derived union ever gains a feature, the `native-probes` feature set would silently stop satisfying the `cfg(all(...))`, the probe test would be compiled out, and the "exact combination" check recorded in `docs/checks/phase-08-rust-1.99.0-native-probes.json` would pass vacuously.
findings.required_fix: Load `contracts/native-exports.json` `probe.requiredFeatures` when building `FEATURES["native-probes"]` in `scripts/check-rust.py`, or add an assertion in `tools/test_ci.py` (alongside `test_every_native_feature_has_an_isolated_job`) that the checker's `native-probes` feature list equals that recorded union.

findings.description: `check_receipt` binds `report["sourceSha256"]` to `source_fingerprint(git_files(root))`, which by the project convention excludes `docs/reviews/`, `docs/checks/` and `docs/phase-status.json` (`tools/review_phase.py:13-14`). The retained receipt was produced at 23:18 (`docs/checks/phase-08-private-material.json:3`), while the final gate report, both package receipts and the live receipt were written afterwards (`docs/checks/phase-08.json:5` 00:20, `phase-08-package-1.99.0.json:3` 00:18). Those newest committed evidence files were therefore never scanned for the selected client identity/secret, and the receipt cannot detect their addition. The limitation is stated honestly at line 27 and in `docs/SECURITY.md:114-117`, so this is a residual coverage gap, not a misstatement; but the standing credential-exclusion evidence does not cover the artifacts most recently added to git.
findings.required_fix: Re-run `python3 scripts/check-private-material.py --config <external> --output <new private path>` as the final step after all phase-8 evidence files are written and replace `docs/checks/phase-08-private-material.json` with that later receipt, or extend the receipt to carry a second fingerprint over the bookkeeping directories so a stale credential scan over check/review artifacts is detectable.

findings.description: MSRV coverage in the executed gate is much narrower than the documented matrix. Locally, 1.89.0 runs only `default`, `minimal`, `all` (inherited from `commands_for(7)`) plus `tracing` and `native-probes` (line 155-157), while 1.99.0 runs 23 feature sets. `docs/CI.md:46` states "Rust 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 each run the complete feature-selection matrix through scripts/check-rust.py", and `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:69-70` does configure both toolchains across all 23 sets — but `docs/phase-status.json` records `remote_ci: configured_unexecuted`, so no evidence exists that isolated product features (`scan`, `management`, `gateway`, `dlp`, `iam`, `model-security`, `red-team`, `agentguard`, `realtime`, `ws-transport`, `reqwest-transport`, `models`, and the JSON/tracing combinations) compile and test at the declared minimum Rust version. `--all-features` at 1.89.0 mitigates most of the risk, since feature-gated code is compiled there in aggregate.
findings.required_fix: Either add the remaining per-feature `scripts/check-rust.py --toolchain 1.89.0` invocations to `commands_for(8)` in `tools/check_phase.py`, or amend `docs/CI.md:46` and `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:63-68` to state that the locally executed MSRV evidence covers default/minimal/all/tracing/native-probes and that the per-isolated-feature MSRV matrix is configured but unexecuted.

findings.description: The generated export-probe consumer declares its own `[workspace]` (line 8), so the root `[workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"` at `Cargo.toml:12-13` does not apply to it, and `contracts/native-probes/src/main.rs` carries no `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. AGENTS.md:11 states that project-owned Rust forbids unsafe code; this crate is project-owned, generated by `tools/native_exports.py`, compiled and executed by `scripts/check-native-exports.py` and copied into the packaged-archive consumer check by `scripts/check-package.py:153-164`. There is no unsafe code in it today (a grep for `unsafe` returns nothing), so this is a policy-enforcement gap rather than a defect.
findings.required_fix: Add `unsafe_code = "forbid"` under a `[lints.rust]` table in `contracts/native-probes/Cargo.toml`, or emit `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in the generated `contracts/native-probes/src/main.rs` header from `tools/native_exports.py`.

findings.description: Two delivery acts named in the phase-8 acceptance evidence are necessarily unverified at review time. Both package receipts record `requireClean: false` and `effectiveDirty: true` (lines 9, 13, 17), i.e. the archives were produced with `--allow-dirty` against an uncommitted tree (~50 modified plus untracked files at `releaseCommit` f72198bd), and `docs/phase-status.json:536-540` records `clean_release_archive: scheduled_after_accepted_source_commit` and no push. `docs/RELEASE.md:29-57` correctly states that an `--allow-dirty` smoke check does not satisfy the clean-commit requirement and that the push follows the accepted commit, and AGENTS.md:13 orders the push after the gate passes — so the sequencing is right and nothing is falsely claimed. Still, "actual package checks" on the released artifact and "push reviewed commits to origin" cannot be evidenced from the current artifacts.
findings.required_fix: After the reviewed source is committed clean, run both `scripts/check-package.py --require-clean` invocations from `docs/RELEASE.md:36-37`, push to `ssh://git@git-ssh.cdot.io/cdot/scm-sdk-rs.git`, and record the pushed commit and the clean archive SHA-256 in `docs/phase-status.json` `delivery` before marking phase 8 complete.

findings.description: This file's layout diverges sharply from its siblings: no spaces around `=` in keyword arguments or dict literals, no space after commas in dict/list literals, and very long single lines (for example lines 20-21, 39, 45-47, 137-145). `scripts/check-rust.py`, `scripts/check-tracing-stress.py` and `scripts/check-private-material.py` all use conventional spacing. Phase 4 and 5 reviews carried an advisory to expand handwritten code layout; this is the one phase-8 script that did not follow it, and it is the script that encodes the release-blocking dependency policy, so readability has direct review value.
findings.required_fix: Reformat `scripts/check-dependencies.py` to match the spacing and line-width conventions used by the other `scripts/check-*.py` runners, keeping the policy logic unchanged.

JSON security boundary verified by reading crates/scm-sdk/src/json_decode.rs in full: guard_wire (120-195) is an allocation-free lexical pre-pass bounded to 512 MiB, depth 128, 1,000,000 nodes and 4× input work, correctly treats any string followed by ':' as a key (covering escaped, duplicate and non-first keys) and caps candidate keys at 6×30 bytes, the exact maximum \u00XX encoding of the longer reserved name; guard_value (197-255) is an iterative stack walk with the same bounds and ensure_supported (48-56) uses crate::validation::discard to avoid a recursive drop on rejection. The only non-test serde_json::from_* calls outside this module are streaming/sse.rs:120 and :144, which read keys as String and values as RawValue/IgnoredAny, and SseEvent::json (sse.rs:61-67) runs json_decode::from_str before raw_error_truthy and json_decode::from_value after, so the guard cannot be bypassed on the SSE path.

Adversarial corpus verified present and executed: crates/scm-sdk/tests/parser_qualification.rs contains exactly the nine tests tabulated in docs/ADVERSARIAL.md:11-24 (exhaustive_short_frame_partitions…, every_two_chunk_split…, fixed_seed_mutations…, malformed_utf8_and_truncation…, event_and_wire_bounds…, lifecycle_json_not_event_name…, overflow_error_envelopes…, cancellation_deadlines_drop_and_close…, empty_chunk_flood_idle_and_transport_errors…), and the jsonBoundaryContract at contracts/qualification.json:25-32 names six reserved-protocol-object tests across json_decode/tests.rs, streaming/sse/tests.rs and tests/gateway_runtime_contracts.rs.

Phase-7 advisories recorded as 'implemented_in_phase_8_pending_review' (docs/phase-status.json:454-464) are in fact implemented: the export-probe gate is derived (tools/native_exports.py:455-456, asserted by tools/test_native_exports.py:121-129); CI MSRV is 1.89.0 (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:36,69); the UUID predicate is centralized at crates/scm-sdk/src/data.rs:324 with thin per-module wrappers (airs/management/mod.rs:144, airs/model_security/mod.rs:41, airs/red_team/common.rs:55, airs/gateway/common.rs:93, airs/scan/scanner.rs:253, validation.rs:1069); and crates/scm-sdk/tests/facade_contracts.rs binds behavioral evidence for Gateway, management/DLP and content accessors rather than compile probes.

Evidence hygiene: every docs/checks/phase-08*.json file corresponds to a gate command output, a preserved failed attempt, or a preserved live attempt — the orphan artifacts flagged in attempt 1 are gone. tools/review_phase.py:13-14,43-60 excludes only docs/reviews/, docs/checks/ and docs/phase-status.json from the source fingerprint, so every docs/*.md guide, script, tool, contract and crate file I read is bound to ce2a547a…. A search for todo!/unimplemented!/FIXME/XXX/HACK across crates/ returns no matches, and Cargo.toml:12-13 sets unsafe_code = "forbid".
limitations: Read-only review: I executed nothing. I verified recorded commands, exit codes, stdout, hashes and artifact contents rather than re-running the 77 gate commands, the dependency audit, the archive extraction, the cross builds, the 100-process stress run or the Rust test suites.

I did not compute the SHA-256 of the reviewed source tree or of docs/checks/phase-08.json myself; I accepted the two values stated in the prompt and cross-checked them against docs/phase-status.json:563, docs/checks/phase-08.json:3, docs/checks/phase-08-private-material.json:4 and docs/checks/phase-08-tracing-stress-1.99.0.json:4, which all agree on ce2a547a….

Phase-8 work is uncommitted (~50 modified plus untracked files at HEAD f72198bd), and I could not run git, so I assessed current file contents rather than a diff against the previously reviewed state.

I spot-read the 1,856-line phase-08.json: the head, the phase-8-specific middle section (lines 1160-1372), and the tail summaries. I confirmed the absence of non-zero exit codes and the exact 77-record count by pattern search rather than reading every record. Likewise I read the qualification matrix's summary, families block and one full operation row rather than all 448 rows.

Child evidence files (26 per-feature rust reports, 4 cross reports, 2 package reports, 2 native-export reports, the dependency report and the live receipt) are not hash-bound into phase-08.json. I verified their summary lines as echoed in the gate stdout and read the dependency, package-1.99.0, private-material, tracing-stress and live-attempt-06 reports directly; I did not open every per-feature rust report.

docs/checks/phase-08-private-material.json deliberately exports no file paths, so I could not independently identify the three git-visible files that contain the selected tenant identifier. The vendored upstream baseline docs under contracts/sources/typescript/docs-site/ do contain vendor TSG-shaped values, which is consistent with the receipt's 'pre-existing HEAD, outside package source' classification, but I could not confirm the specific files.

I did not read .local/typescript or any credential/tenant-registration file, so the frozen-baseline parity figures (2,630 root exports, 448 methods, 3,820 capabilities, 1,086 public schemas) rest on the recorded extractor/oracle stdout and the tooling's own self-tests, not on independent inspection of the TypeScript source.

I cannot determine whether the two reproducible 400 responses originate in the SDK or the service; that is precisely the open question in my medium finding, and no artifact in the repository resolves it.
